summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted with a dehisced right above-knee amputation stump and malodorous drainage. She had a history of Proteus mirabilis and Klebsiella pneumoniae infections, and outpatient imipenem was continued. Wound cultures during admission confirmed Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus, with sensitivity to daptomycin, which was added before discharge. She underwent bedside debridements to promote healthy granulation tissue and received a vacuum-assisted closure device. Her dialysis schedule was maintained, and she was managed on Coumadin with heparin bridging. Hyponatremia was addressed with a 1.5 L fluid restriction. She remained afebrile with improving infection markers and was discharged to extended care for ongoing IV antibiotics, wound care, and rehabilitation.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
